llm.reason: Team.id and Player_Attributes.id are unrelated primary keys from different ID pools (Player_Attributes ids are a dense 1..183978 sequence of player-attribute rows), and a team cannot be a kind of player-attribute record, so the full containment with 0.002 coverage is coincidental.
A country is not a kind of match; the 11 country IDs merely fall inside Match's 1..25979 key range, so the overlap is coincidental.
A league is not a kind of match, and the overlap of 11 league ids with 25979 sequential match ids is coincidental small-integer overlap (Match has its own league_id column for the real reference).
League.id exactly reuses the country ID pool (identical profiles, full coverage, league names match country names), showing League is a per-country extension keyed by the country's ID.

League.country_id values exactly match Country.id (full containment and coverage), and sample rows align semantically (England Premier League → England, Germany 1. Bundesliga → Germany), so this is the real reference.
League.id exactly equals Country.id (sample rows show id identical to country_id, full containment and coverage), so each league id genuinely identifies its country, a real one-to-one reference.
Match.id is a match identifier with 25979 rows and zero coverage of the 11 league country ids; the overlap is coincidental and a league's country_id cannot reference a match.
League.country_id has full containment and coverage of Country.id and its values demonstrably name the same countries (England, Germany, Portugal), so it is a genuine foreign key.

Match.id is a synthetic match row identifier (1..25979), not a team ID; the overlap with team_api_id is coincidental small-integer overlap, and the real reference Team.team_api_id is already accepted.
Player.id is a synthetic player row identifier (1..11075), not a team ID; team_api_id cannot reference a player, so the overlap is coincidental.

away_team_api_id references teams (already accepted to Team.team_api_id), and its overlap with Player.id is coincidental small-integer ID collision with no semantic link between a team and a player row.
home_team_api_id holds team API IDs (already accepted to Team.team_api_id), and its overlap with Player.id is coincidental small-integer ID collision between unrelated ID pools (teams vs players).

The source holds FIFA team IDs while the target is a surrogate row ID for player-attribute snapshots (different entities), and the full containment with 0.002 coverage is just small-integer overlap by chance.

Player_Attributes.id is a surrogate row key for player-attribute snapshots; its overlap with away_team_api_id is chance overlap of small integers, not a reference from a match's away team to a player attribute row.
Player_Attributes.id is a per-attribute-row surrogate key, and its near-total containment of team IDs is a chance overlap of dense integer ranges, not a reference from a team column.
